slides.0.title: White grape varieties
slides.0.subtitle: Grüner Veltliner, Riesling and others
slides.1.title: Grüner Veltliner: the flagship
slides.1.highlights.0.title: The key white grape
slides.1.highlights.0.content: About one third of the vineyard area (32.3% in 2025)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Weinviertel is the heartland
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Weinviertel holds about half of the country's Grüner Veltliner (Wikipedia)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Style profile
slides.1.highlights.2.content: White pepper, citrus and green apple with medium-plus acidity; from light and fresh to rich, age-worthy styles such as Wachau Smaragd
slides.1.content: Always give the year; the takeaway is "about one third".
slides.2.title: Riesling and Welschriesling
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Riesling
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Best on the steep slopes and primary-rock soils of Wachau, Kamptal and Kremstal, tight, mineral and high in acidity
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Welschriesling is not Riesling
slides.2.highlights.1.content: The two are unrelated; Welschriesling is neutral with high acidity (about 6.3% of the area in 2025)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: What Welschriesling is used for
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Often used for Burgenland's botrytised sweet wines, and also for Sekt and light dry wines
slides.2.content: Similar names but two different varieties — a classic trap question.
slides.3.title: Other important whites
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Weißburgunder and Chardonnay
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Weißburgunder is Pinot Blanc; Chardonnay in Steiermark is often called Morillon
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Sauvignon Blanc and Gelber Muskateller
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Especially well known in Steiermark, with vivid aromas and high acidity
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Rotgipfler and Zierfandler
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Local specialities of the Thermenregion, often blended together into rich styles
slides.3.highlights.3.title: Others
slides.3.highlights.3.content: Müller-Thurgau, Neuburger, Frühroter Veltliner, Muscat Ottonel and the Traminer family are also grown
slides.3.content: The list is long; start with the ones most likely to be examined.
slides.4.title: Style cheat sheet
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Grüner Veltliner
slides.4.highlights.0.content: White pepper, citrus, green apple; medium-plus acidity; light to rich
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Riesling
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Peach, citrus, minerality; high acidity; mostly dry
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Welschriesling
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Neutral and high in acidity; suited to base wines and sweet wines
slides.4.highlights.3.title: Sauvignon Blanc (Steiermark)
slides.4.highlights.3.content: Grass, blackcurrant leaf and tropical fruit; high acidity
slides.4.content: In a blind tasting, "white pepper plus citrus" points first to Grüner Veltliner.
slides.5.title: Diploma depth: Grüner Veltliner’s origins and viticulture
slides.5.highlights.0.title: Parents: Traminer × St. Georgener-Rebe
slides.5.highlights.0.content: DNA work in the late 1990s identified Traminer (Savagnin) as one parent; the other was found only in 2000 as a single surviving old vine in St. Georgen, Burgenland, and named St. Georgener-Rebe (sources date the confirmation to 2007 or 2009; not tested). It has no known link to the other “Veltliner” varieties
slides.5.highlights.1.title: Vigorous and high-yielding: quality depends on yield control
slides.5.highlights.1.content: Grüner is vigorous and naturally high-yielding; left alone it gives thin, neutral wine. The concentration of Smaragd or Ried wines comes from low yields and later picking. The Diploma causal chain: yield → concentration → style tier → price
slides.5.highlights.2.title: Prefers deep loess, dislikes drought
slides.5.highlights.2.content: Loess holds water and lets roots go deep, which is why it is Grüner’s classic soil (Wagram, Weinviertel, lower Wachau); on thin primary rock the vine suffers water stress. In the drier years that climate change brings, water stress is one of Grüner’s biggest viticultural risks
slides.5.highlights.3.title: Where the white pepper comes from
slides.5.highlights.3.content: Grüner’s white-pepper note is commonly linked to the sesquiterpene rotundone (also behind Syrah’s black pepper); cooler vintages and sites usually show more pepper. This is a research association whose strength varies by vintage and site: a tendency, not a rule
slides.5.content: In essays, tie variety traits to style: vigour → yield control; loess → water; cool → pepper.
Roughly what share of Austria's vineyard area is Grüner Veltliner?
About 32.3% in 2025, making it the leading white variety.
What is the relationship between Welschriesling and Riesling?
A. Two names for the same variety
C. Welschriesling is a Riesling offspring
D. Welschriesling is a red grape
The names are similar but the varieties are unrelated.
Which variety is called Morillon in Steiermark?
Morillon is Steiermark's name for Chardonnay.
